correctness.rationale: The precise open-neighborhood identity gives total domination iff a,b>=2 and locating all outside vertices iff at most one matching pair is completely omitted. Multinomial counting gives each coefficient, inclusion-exclusion yields the univariate polynomial, and deletion arguments show every inclusion-minimal set has size max(4,n-1). The 349504 subset exhaustive original-definition checks through n=9 corroborate but do not replace the proof.

value.rationale: The crown graph is a canonical vertex-transitive, matching-deleted complete bipartite family. The theorem determines the full all-size and part-refined distribution and characterizes every inclusion-minimal solution. The unexpectedly strong rigidity (all inclusion-minimal solutions minimum) with exponential labeled multiplicity yields meaningful structural information unavailable from general location-total bounds.
